sentences.text: Addl. Chief Secy. Home Police Anubhag-6 Civil Sectt. Lk

Counsel for Petitioner :- Deepak Singh
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Manish Mathur,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for petitioner and learned State Counsel appearing on behalf of opposite parties.
2. Petition has been filed seeking a direction to the opposite parties to permit petitioner to appear in a written test for his consideration for appointment on compassionate grounds.

3. It has been submitted that petitioner's father late Chhabi Lal Prasad passed away in service on 3rd July, 2018 on the post of Head Constable Civil Police whereafter petitioner sought compassionate appointment.

Petitioner participated in the physical test where he was declared successful Sanjay Prasad Alias Sanjay Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl.Chief Secy. ... on 18 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149032350/
1 whereafter a written test was to be held on 5th September, 2021 but petitioner could not appear for the same since he was incarcerated in pursuance of case crime No. 165 of 2021 instituted against him under section 376 IPC.

entities.text: Sanjay Prasad Alias Sanjay Kumar vs State Of U.P. Thru. Addl.Chief Secy
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further submitted that petitioner was thereafter enlarged on bail vide order dated 27th November, 2021 but due to his earlier incarceration, he could not appear in written examination and now seeks permission for same.

4. Learned State Counsel on the basis of instructions however submits that in terms of government order dated 18th September, 2015, the petitioner has already been granted an opportunity to appear in written examination and there is no provision for any further entitlement of petitioner to appear in the written examination.

5. However it is quite evident from submissions of learned counsel for petitioner that he had qualified the physical test but was unable to appear in written examination on account of his incarceration which would have rendered his appearance in written examination impossible.

Although the aforesaid government order may not provide for a subsequent written examination but it is nonetheless an admitted fact that petitioner's father passed away while in service and petitioner was entitled to be considered for compassionate appointment.
6. For the said grievance petitioner has already submitted a representation but seeks liberty to file a fresh representation before the concerned authority.

7. In view innocuous prayer being made by learned counsel for the petitioner and without entering into the merits of the case petitioner is granted liberty to make a fresh representation for appearance in written examination pursuant to his earlier application for compassionate appointment.

In case such a representation is made, the opposite party No.3 or any other concerned authority shall consider and decide petitioner's representation in case there is no specific bar in petitioner's further participation in written examination.
8. With the aforesaid observations, the writ petition stands disposed of.
